The rodent problem in our residential neighborhoods has gotten completely out of hand. Rats are showing up in yards, under porches, and even near entryways in broad daylight, and it’s becoming way too close for comfort. Families shouldn’t have to worry about their kids playing outside or their pets getting exposed to disease, yet that’s exactly what’s happening. Garden beds, stored materials, and outdoor spaces are being torn apart, and it’s clear the situation isn’t just an inconvenience anymore — it’s a health and safety issue.

At this point, the city needs to step in with real, visible action. The infestation is growing faster than residents can manage on their own, and without coordinated efforts like targeted rodent control, better waste management enforcement, and neighborhood‑level mitigation plans, the problem will only keep spreading. People deserve to feel safe in and around their homes, and right now, that’s not the case.
